newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt releases 105,000 T French wheat held at port.
newsitem.headline: Egypt releases 105,000 T French wheat held at port.

text.p: The Egyptian state's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) said on Tuesday that 105,000 tonnes of French wheat had been cleared at Port Said despite an unusually high proportion of foreign matter.
"It is not rejected," GASC vice chairman Samir Shakankiri told Reuters. "This wheat has been released. There are some defects but I would like to stress -- no rejection."

Harbour authorities at Port Said said on Sunday that a first consignment of 52,500 tonnes of French wheat contained more than one percent stones and gravel. A second consignment of the same amount had the same problem, but to a lesser extent, they said.
But Shakankiri said only about 20,000 tonnes, all from the first consignment, was affected and that all the wheat would be fit for human consumption.
"We shall sieve it or something like that," he added.
GASC would seek compensation for the defects, Shakankiri said. GASC bought the wheat from Soufflet and the consignment was inspected in Dunkirk by SGS, he added.
He said there was no problem with a third consignment of 52,500 tonnes arriving aboard the cargo ship Vancouver from Dunkirk and Rouen. --Jonathan Wright +202 578 3290/91
